blocks.text: Federated learning lets many clients train a shared model without sharing raw data. However, clients may free ride by contributing little while still receiving the global model. This paper studies how to detect free riding.
Prior work assumes honest participation. We relax this assumption and model each client as a rational agent that chooses its own training effort.
We propose a truthful mechanism that rewards clients in proportion to their verified contribution.

The server estimates each contribution by comparing the submitted update with a held-out validation gradient. Clients whose updates have low alignment receive a smaller reward. The reward rule is monotone in alignment, so exaggerating effort never helps. We prove that truthful reporting is a dominant strategy under mild conditions.
We evaluate on CIFAR-10 and FEMNIST with one hundred simulated clients. Thirty percent of the clients free ride.
